confidence.reason: Source trace is complete and the missing timeout is visible on every failure and success path; socket-hang duration was not measured because target execution was unavailable.

description: The hosted Turnstile verification path performs an outbound HTTPS POST to Cloudflare siteverify without a socket timeout. The vulnerable call is reachable from an unauthenticated endpoint, POST /api/auth/login/start, before any authenticated session is required.

evidence.description: httplib2.Http() is constructed with no timeout argument, unlike TOKEN_TIMEOUT_SECONDS used for Google token calls.
The no-timeout response is used as the sole pass/fail gate for login initiation.
Callers propagate the unbounded result without adding their own time bound.
Google token exchange in the same codebase uses an explicit 30-second timeout, establishing that unbounded outbound calls are not the intended pattern.

instructions: Configure hosted mode with Turnstile enabled.
POST /api/auth/login/start with an attacker-chosen token while Cloudflare siteverify is slow or unresponsive.
Observe that the affected request thread remains occupied for the duration of the outbound socket wait.
Repeat with a small number of concurrent unauthenticated requests and observe shared request-handling capacity being retained.
execution.observed_result: Each affected login-start request retains its worker while waiting on siteverify; sustained slow responses retain shared request-handling capacity.

intended_behavior: Unauthenticated outbound verification calls should have an explicit low timeout and fail closed, so a slow verification provider cannot retain shared request-handling capacity.

remediation.strategy: Add an explicit low timeout to the Turnstile siteverify POST and keep fail-closed behavior; use the same bounded-transport pattern already used by oauth_transport.

root_cause: Missing outbound timeout on the Cloudflare Turnstile siteverify POST in _verify_turnstile.

impact.reason: Shared request-handling capacity can be retained by slow verification responses; no credential, tenant-data, or code-execution boundary is crossed.

likelihood.reason: The affected endpoint is unauthenticated and the timeout is absent on every call, but exploitation needs sustained slow siteverify responses and competes with existing per-IP login throttling.

title: Turnstile siteverify POST has no outbound timeout

trace.description: Unauthenticated entry: login-start endpoint enabled only with Turnstile keys.
Attacker-controlled token is passed to verification.
Verification helper performs an outbound HTTPS POST.
HTTP client is created without a timeout; unbounded socket wait.
